headline: Fed's Barr says AI agents could speed up bank runs
body: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said at a conference in Milan on November 16 that AI agents may accelerate deposit outflows during stress periods, potentially accelerating runs that unfold in minutes. He said major banks now report finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts, without the bank being able to verify authenticity, consent, and alignment with customer instructions.
note: Barr's list of guardrails (strict authentication, explicit consent checks and limits on agent capabilities) gives banks a checklist for how they handle agent access to customer accounts.

evidence.text: In addition, AI agents may accelerate deposit outflows during stress periods.

Where customers once needed to execute transfers, AI agents could instantaneously detect yield differentials or stability signals and autonomously move funds at high speed, potentially accelerating runs that unfold in minutes, overwhelming traditional liquidity management and regulatory intervention timelines.

For example, major banks now report finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts, without the bank being able to verify authenticity, consent, and alignment with customer instructions.

These incidents underscore that AI in financial services can only succeed long term with appropriate guardrails: strict authentication, explicit consent verification for specific actions, technical controls limiting agent capabilities, and both rules- and values-based constraints.
At the Seventh Annual Association for Computing Machinery International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Finance, Milan, Italy
